content.overview: BNS s. 59 — Public servant concealing design to commit offence which it is his duty to prevent.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Public servant concealing design to commit offence which it is his duty to prevent. BNS restatement of IPC 119. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 119. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 59 is the rule on “Public servant concealing design to commit offence which it is his duty to prevent”. The section provides that whoever, being a public servant, intending to facilitate or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby facilitate the commission of an offence which it is his duty as such public servant to prevent, voluntarily conceals, by any act or omission or by the use of encryption or any other information hiding tool, the existence of a design to commit such offence, or makes any representation which he knows to be false respecting such design shall,–. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 59 exists so that “Public servant concealing design to commit offence which it is his duty to prevent” has a closed legal test in Chapter IV — Of Abetment, Criminal Conspiracy and Attempt. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: The inchoate trio. Abetment now covers extra-territorial aid; conspiracy and attempt sit next to it.

The provision in detail
59. Whoever, being a public servant, intending to facilitate or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby facilitate the commission of an offence which it is his duty as such public servant to prevent, voluntarily conceals, by any act or omission or by the use of encryption or any other information hiding tool, the existence of a design to commit such offence, or makes any representation which he knows to be false respecting such design shall,–

(a) if the offence be committed, be punished with imprisonment of any description provided for the offence, for a term which may extend to one-half of the longest term of such imprisonment, or with such fine as is provided for that offence, or with both; or

(b) if the offence be punishable with death or imprisonment for life, with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years; or

(c) if the offence be not committed, shall be punished with imprisonment of any description provided for the offence for a term which may extend to one-fourth part of the longest term of such imprisonment or with such fine as is provided for the offence, or with both

Essential ingredients
1. Whoever, being a public servant, intending to facilitate or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby facilitate the commission of an offence which it is his duty as such public servant to prevent, voluntarily conceals, by any act or omission or by the use of encryption or any other information hiding tool, the existence of a design to commit such offence, or makes any representation which he knows to be false respecting such design shall,–
2. (a) if the offence be committed, be punished with imprisonment of any description provided for the offence, for a term which may extend to one-half of the longest term of such imprisonment, or with such fine as is provided for that offence, or with both; or
3. (b) if the offence be punishable with death or imprisonment for life, with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years; or
4. (c) if the offence be not committed, shall be punished with imprisonment of any description provided for the offence for a term which may extend to one-fourth part of the longest term of such imprisonment or with such fine as is provided for the offence, or with both

Statutory illustrations
Illustration (a). A, an officer of police, being legally bound to give information of all designs to commit robbery which may come to his knowledge, and knowing that B designs to commit robbery, omits to give such information, with intent to so facilitate the commission of that offence

Exam use: quote illustration (a), then write which ingredient of BNS s. 59 it proves. Copying the illustration without that mapping sentence does not score.

Illustration (b). Here A has by an illegal omission concealed the existence of B’s design, and is liable to punishment according to the provision of this section

Exam use: quote illustration (b), then write which ingredient of BNS s. 59 it proves. Copying the illustration without that mapping sentence does not score.
